To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

LLM from styloid and porcupine vetch joint can be used as CP sources in the diet of Lao pigs, and that the use of LLM from stylosanthes and porcupine-joint vetch as protein sources for Lao pigs can be recommended as it can replace soybean meal and improve the use of feed resources.

the replacement of soybean protein with legume leaf protein from porcupines and stylo in the diet of Lao pigs reduced feed intake, growth and carcass traits, and that supplementation of the traditional diet with soybean meal increased feed intake and growth and carcass performance.

the replacement of soybean protein with porcupine joint-vetch (Aeschynome histrix BRA 9689) and Stylosanthes leaf meal in the diets of growing native female (Moo Lao) Lao pigs resulted in a linear reduction of feed intake, average daily gain and carcass weight and a linear increase of feed conversion ratio.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of replacing soy protein with protein from LLM from stylosanthes and porcupine vetch on the growth performance and carcasses of native female Moo Lanth Lao pigs.
the use of legume leaf meals as a protein source in the diets of growing native Lao pigs.
the effect of replacing soy protein with legume leaf protein on the growth performance of native female Moo Lanth Lao pigs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LLM from stylosanthes and porcupine vetch can be utilized as a protein source to partially replace SBM in the diet of native Lao female pigs.
the LLM can be used as protein source for pigs but the level of inclusion should be limited to 33 % of the soybean protein.
the use of LLM from stylos and porcupine vetch can be considered as a protein source to partially replace the soybean protein in the diet of native female Moo Laths Lao pigs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LLM can be used to reduce the amount of imported soybean meal in the feed of native female Moo Lanth Lao pigs.
the LLM can be used as an economical protein source for native female Lao pigs.
the Lao pigs can be fed with the legume leaf meal as a protein source instead of soybean meal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LLM can be used as an alternative protein source for soybean meal in native female Moo Lat Lao pig diets.
Lao pigs can be fed diets with a high proportion of legume leaf meal, but the inclusion rate should not exceed 33 % of soybean protein in the diet.
the use of LLM as a source of protein in the diets of native female Moo Latham pigs is possible.
